A.explanation: This fixes the volume to one cubic metre, so it describes a mass in $\text{kg}$ rather than the general ratio $\rho = m/V$.

B.explanation: This describes the mass contained in one unit of volume but does not state density as mass divided by volume.

C.explanation: This fixes the unit to per cubic metre, which gives the SI unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ rather than the general definition.

D.explanation: This states the defining ratio $\rho = m/V$ as mass divided by volume for any unit system.

hints: Look closely at the wording change between one cubic metre, per cubic metre and unit volume across options A to D.
Recall $\rho = m/V$ where $m$ is mass and $V$ is volume, so the word per means divided by.
Ask which phrase stays correct if volume is measured in $\text{cm}^3$ or $\text{m}^3$ and still expresses a mass to volume ratio.
walkthrough: Identify what is tested: the general definition linking mass $m$ and volume $V$, not a value in a particular unit.
State the governing relation $\rho = m/V$, where density $\rho$ is mass divided by volume.
Translate the mathematics into words: divided by volume is written as per unit volume, which applies to any choice of volume unit.
Compare the cubic metre options: mass of one cubic metre and mass per cubic metre both fix the volume unit to $\text{m}^3$, so they describe the SI case only.
Select the wording that gives the ratio for any unit volume without fixing it to $\text{m}^3$. This is option D.
